questions.question: When inspecting the inside of a bus, you should:

options.text: Remove the emergency exit handles.
Assume all buzzers work properly.
Make sure all seats are fastened securely.
Skip checking the handrails and floor lining.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure all seats are fastened securely.
questions.explanation: When inspecting the inside of a bus, check that everything is safe and works properly. Make sure all seats are firmly attached to the bus and safe for passengers.

questions.question: When carrying multiple types of approved hazardous materials on a bus, you may carry no more than a combined total of ____ at one time.

options.text: 10 pounds
50 pounds
100 pounds
500 pounds

questions.correctAnswerText: 500 pounds
questions.explanation: Buses can carry no more than 500 pounds total of hazardous materials. This includes no more than 100 pounds of any single type of material.

questions.question: During a bus ride:

options.text: Carry-on bags may be kept in the aisle.
Passengers may sit in the aisle.
Aisles must be kept clear of objects.
Small items can stay in the aisle if passengers can step over them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Aisles must be kept clear of objects.
questions.explanation: Do not allow baggage in doorways or aisles. Nothing should be in the aisle that could cause someone to trip. Store baggage securely to prevent damage.

questions.question: Hazardous materials must be marked with all of the following, except:

options.text: The material's name.
The material's ID number.
The correct hazard label.
A contact person's phone number.

questions.correctAnswerText: A contact person's phone number.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials must show the material's name, ID number, and hazard label. Only transport hazardous materials if you are sure they are allowed.

questions.question: When inspecting the inside of a bus, you should:

options.text: Loosen every seat.
Check every handhold.
Assume all buzzers work properly.
Remove the emergency exit handles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check every handhold.
questions.explanation: When inspecting the inside of a bus, make sure everything is safe and in good condition. Check that all handholds and railings are firmly in place and safe to use.

questions.question: At railroad crossings, bus drivers:

options.text: Do not need to stop.
Do not need to stop, but must slow down 25 mph below the posted speed.
Do not need to stop, but must open the door to listen for trains.
Must stop and check for approaching trains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop and check for approaching trains.
questions.explanation: When approaching a railroad crossing in a bus, stop 15 to 50 feet before the nearest track. Look and listen for trains. Only go forward when you are sure no trains are coming. You do not need to stop at streetcar crossings, when directed by a police officer, at green traffic lights, or at crossings marked "exempt" or "abandoned."

questions.question: When approaching a drawbridge with a traffic signal, you may proceed:

options.text: If the signal is green.
Only after stopping completely 50 feet before the bridge.
Only if other vehicles are also going across.
Only after getting out to check conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: If the signal is green.
questions.explanation: If a drawbridge has a traffic signal showing green, you may slow down and go without stopping.

questions.question: On a bus, the driver:

options.text: Does not have to wear a seat belt, but it is recommended.
Must wear a seat belt.
Should not wear a seat belt.
Must wear a seat belt only if licensed for less than one year.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must wear a seat belt.
questions.explanation: The driver's seat on a bus should have a seat belt. Always wear it.

questions.question: You should sign a previous driver's inspection report if:

options.text: The previous driver dated their entry.
Any reported defects have been repaired.
You plan to drive more than one hour or travel more than 50 miles.
The report is on the dashboard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any reported defects have been repaired.
questions.explanation: Only sign a previous inspection report if defects were either fixed or if no repairs were needed.

questions.question: Bus accidents happen most often:

options.text: At intersections.
On highways.
On rural roads.
In parking garages.

questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections.
questions.explanation: Bus accidents happen most often at intersections. Be extra careful where there are many vehicles and pedestrians.

questions.question: Before driving a bus that has been parked for a few days, what should you do?

options.text: Assume the interior is in good working order.
Call the local police department.
Walk through the bus to check for any damage.
Ask passengers to check the interior of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk through the bus to check for any damage.
questions.explanation: Unattended buses can be damaged. Before driving a bus that has been parked, check the interior to make sure everything is in good condition.

questions.question: When inspecting the inside of a bus, you should:

options.text: Assume all emergency exits work properly.
Loosen every seat.
Test all signaling devices.
Skip checking the handrails and floor.

questions.correctAnswerText: Test all signaling devices.
questions.explanation: When you inspect the inside of a bus, you must check that everything is safe and works properly. Test all signaling devices, like emergency buzzers in the bathroom.

questions.question: Buses should never carry:

options.text: Medical drugs.
Small arms ammunition.
Emergency hospital supplies.
Radioactive materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Radioactive materials.
questions.explanation: Buses must never carry labeled radioactive materials where passengers sit. Small arms ammunition labeled ORM-D, emergency hospital supplies, and medications are allowed.

questions.question: When stopping at a railroad crossing, opening the front door:

options.text: Helps you hear an approaching train.
Should never be done.
Lets in noise that makes it harder to hear trains.
Takes too long and is not recommended.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps you hear an approaching train.
questions.explanation: When you stop a bus at a railroad crossing, open the front door if it helps you see or hear a train coming.

questions.question: Baggage and freight on a bus should be stored to:

options.text: Let passengers easily see the items.
Protect passengers if items fall or move.
Keep items in the aisle without moving.
Cover the windows.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect passengers if items fall or move.
questions.explanation: Baggage and freight must be stored so the driver can move freely, passengers can exit through any window or door in an emergency, and passengers are protected if items fall or shift.

questions.question: Before operating a bus, you should check that it is safe by:

options.text: Reading the inspection report from the previous driver.
Kicking the tires.
Asking your supervisor if the bus seems safe.
Asking passengers if they are comfortable.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reading the inspection report from the previous driver.
questions.explanation: A bus must be inspected before you drive it. You must review the inspection report from the previous driver. Only operate the bus if any problems listed have been fixed or do not need to be fixed.

questions.question: A bus driver does not need to stop when approaching:

options.text: A raised drawbridge.
A streetcar crossing.
A railroad crossing.
A stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: A streetcar crossing.
questions.explanation: When approaching a railroad crossing, you must stop 15 to 50 feet from the nearest track to look and listen for trains. Only drive forward when you are sure no trains are coming. You do not need to stop at streetcar crossings, when a police officer is directing traffic, when a green traffic signal is showing, or at crossings marked "exempt" or "abandoned."

questions.question: On a bus, the driver:

options.text: Does not need to wear a seat belt.
Must always wear a seat belt.
Must wear a seat belt only during school hours.
Must wear a seat belt only if licensed for less than a year.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must always wear a seat belt.
questions.explanation: A bus driver seat must have a seat belt, and the driver must always wear it.

questions.question: When inspecting the inside of a bus, you should:

options.text: Skip checking the handrails and floor.
Make sure seats are loosely attached.
Assume all buzzers work.
Make sure emergency exits are easy to use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure emergency exits are easy to use.
questions.explanation: When you inspect the inside of a bus, check that everything is safe and works properly. Make sure emergency exits are clearly marked and easy to use.

questions.question: Buses must never carry:

options.text: Small arms ammunition.
Soft drinks.
Medical supplies.
Tear gas.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tear gas.
questions.explanation: Some hazardous materials can be carried on a bus under certain conditions, but tear gas and irritating materials can never be carried. Small arms ammunition labeled ORM-D and emergency medical supplies are permitted.
